headline: FULA Network Hits 26 Nodes as AI-Storage Convergence Heats Up
subtitle: Functionland's controlled AI file-access feature arrives as MCP security concerns reshape how the industry thinks about agent permissions.
briefing: Functionland's FULA network has grown to 26 active nodes — up from 24 the prior week — a steady climb that underscores the community-driven momentum behind the project. More strategically significant is the FxFiles MCP integration announced earlier this month, which lets users invite an AI assistant into a single designated folder, with read and write access but no delete permissions. That design choice is well-timed. <cite index="26-2,26-7">The Model Context Protocol gives AI agents access to real systems — file systems, databases, APIs — with real consequences, and it is also a new and serious attack surface.</cite> A CISA advisory on MCP security published in June 2026 flagged vulnerabilities in a significant fraction of publicly available MCP servers, making Functionland's least-privilege, folder-scoped approach a credible differentiator. The broader DePIN tailwind remains strong: <cite index="9-9">as of May 2026, CoinMarketCap tracks 265 DePIN tokens with a combined market cap of approximately $18.92 billion.</cite> Within that sector, <cite index="2-11">leading DePIN networks generated roughly $150 million in on-chain revenue in January 2026 alone</cite>, signaling that paying demand — not just speculation — is driving growth. <cite index="16-13">Functionland's roadmap targets Q2 2026 for migrating larger organizations' data from traditional cloud to the Fula ecosystem</cite>, a move that, if executed, could materially expand the network's utility case. Watch for node count acceleration and enterprise onboarding announcements as the most concrete proof points in the months ahead.
